title: Day 684: Man Chased on Foot and Shot Dead in Nueva Galicia, Culiacán — Early Morning Targeted Killing, Foot Pursuit Leaves Sneakers Behind
detail:
On Day 684 of the Sinaloa cartel civil war — June 7, 2026, at approximately 5:30 AM — an unidentified adult male (approximately 35–40 years old, bald, with tattoos on his back) was chased on foot by at least one attacker through the Fraccionamiento Nueva Galicia neighborhood in southern Culiacán and shot multiple times in the head. The victim's sneakers were found abandoned at a distance from the body, indicating he had been forced to flee on foot before being overtaken. The chase-and-execution pattern is characteristic of targeted narco-retribution killings.

Mexican Army and municipal preventive police responded to the scene. The Fiscalía General del Estado (FGE) opened an investigation. No faction claimed the killing; the foot-pursuit execution method is used by both Chapitos and La Mayiza factions in urban Culiacán.

The killing occurred the morning after at least two other violent incidents on June 6 (the Valle Alto water purification business attack: 1 dead; and the Urbivilla del Roble food delivery driver killing). The continued pace of early-morning targeted killings indicates that neither the Murciélagos special forces deployment (Day 680, June 3) nor the emergency supervisory visit by the Defense Secretary and National Guard Commander (Day 681, June 4) has interrupted the Chapitos–La Mayiza operational tempo in Culiacán's residential neighborhoods.

title: Day 684: Mexican Army Ocelotl Unit Secures Explosives Cache in El Rosario After Residents Report Five Blasts — Southern Sinaloa Conflict Persists
detail:
On the evening of June 6, 2026, residents of the Infonavit Lola Beltrán neighborhood in El Rosario, Sinaloa, reported at least five explosions beginning at approximately 7:00 PM. The Mexican Army's Ocelotl unit (elite counter-cartel force) responded alongside state and municipal police, cordoning off a residential property where explosive material was allegedly discovered. The property was secured and held pending investigation; the incident was reported by Noroeste on the morning of June 7.

OCELOTL DEPLOYMENT SIGNIFICANCE: The deployment of the Ocelotl unit to El Rosario — rather than standard security forces — indicates the suspected cartel connection to the explosives cache. Ocelotl is a specialized SEDENA counter-narcotics force assigned to Sinaloa for targeted operations against cartel infrastructure. The unit's presence in El Rosario confirms that federal security operations are extending from the Culiacán epicenter to the southernmost conflict municipalities.

EL ROSARIO CONTEXT: El Rosario municipality has been a persistent conflict zone throughout the civil war. In May 2026, the recently arrested Chapitos plaza boss 'El Gabito' (Gabriel Nicolás Martínez Larios, arrested June 1 in Mazatlán) left a narco banner with two dismembered bodies in El Rosario days before his arrest — claiming rejection of a defection offer from La Mayiza. The explosives cache incident suggests ongoing cartel armed activity in the southern Sinaloa corridor, consistent with Escuinapa municipality's documented 14 consecutive days of gunfire and explosions through June 6. El Rosario borders Nayarit state, a strategically important gateway for trafficking routes toward Guadalajara.

title: Day 684: Infobae Analysis — CJNG Gunmen Documented on Google Street View at Tepuche Checkpoint Northwest of Culiacán, Confirming Los Chapitos Alliance Operationally Active
detail:
On June 7, 2026, Infobae published a detailed analysis of Google Street View imagery documenting an armed CJNG checkpoint in the community of Los Algodones (Tepuche sector) northwest of Culiacán, where six gunmen carrying AK-47-pattern rifles stopped and inspected the Google mapping vehicle. At least one gunman wore a CJNG-marked tactical vest ('Fuerzas Especiales Unión' insignia). The images remained visible on Google Maps for approximately one year after capture — testament to the operational brazenness of the CJNG-Chapitos alliance at the time of filming.

INFOBAE ANALYSIS (June 7, 2026): Infobae presented the Street View documentation as visual confirmation of the Los Chapitos–CJNG operational alliance in Culiacán's hinterland, noting that the alliance's key facilitator — Audias Flores Silva 'El Jardinero' (El Mencho's head of security) — was arrested by Mexican forces in Nayarit on April 27, 2026 (US offered $5M reward). His removal eliminated the operational military commander most directly responsible for CJNG's Sinaloa deployments. Los Chapitos' principal leaders — Iván Archivaldo Guzmán Salazar and Jesús Alfredo 'El Mochomito' Guzmán Salazar — remain at large with $10M US rewards each.

CHECKPOINT SIGNIFICANCE: The Tepuche corridor northwest of Culiacán (along the El Fuerte highway) has been a documented CJNG-Chapitos forward deployment zone throughout the civil war. The visual evidence of six armed CJNG fighters conducting vehicle inspections on a public road — with impunity sufficient to allow Google's mapping vehicle to pass and record — illustrates the extent of extra-state territorial control by the allied factions. The Street View documentation is now analytical evidence alongside InSight Crime field reporting and Proceso investigations on the alliance.
